html:
The Munich Agreement was signed in Munich early on 30 September 1938 by Germany, Britain, France and Italy, allowing Nazi Germany to annex the Sudetenland, the German speaking border areas of Czechoslovakia.

Hitler had threatened war over the Sudeten Germans. The British prime minister Neville Chamberlain and France's Édouard Daladier agreed to his demands to avoid it. Czechoslovakia, which had an alliance with France and strong border forts, was not invited. Chamberlain said he had brought back peace for our time. Czechoslovakia lost its defences and much industry, and in March 1939 Germany occupied the rest of the Czech lands. Czechs call it the Munich betrayal, and the word Munich became shorthand for appeasement. Six months later Hitler turned to Poland, starting World War II.
sum: The Munich Agreement was signed in Munich early on 30 September 1938 by Germany, Britain, France and Italy, allowing Nazi Germany to annex the Sudetenland, the German speaking border areas of Czechoslovakia.
